topic_description: When the heart says thank you
disclaimer: This topic is for reflection and spiritual growth. It is not a substitute for professional care.

reassurance_anchor.text_en: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.

verses.translation_en: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does 'Shukr' mean?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It comes from SH-K-R. In the Quran, it is more than words. It is recognition, and it is action.

evidence.arabic: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا
evidence.translation_en: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them.
evidence.why_cited: It shows the greatness of what is given.

evidence.arabic: فَاذْكُرُونِي أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِي وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ
evidence.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does increase mean here?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It is open. It is not limited. The verse does not specify what will be increased.

evidence.translation_en: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
evidence.why_cited: It leaves the increase open, without limit.

evidence.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you.
evidence.why_cited: It shows increase begins with remembrance.

verses.arabic_text: فَاذْكُرُونِي أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِي وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ
verses.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What is the link between remembrance and gratitude?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: The verse joins them. Remembering leads to gratitude. Gratitude flows from remembrance.

evidence.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me.
If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
evidence.why_cited: It shows gratitude leads to increase.

verses.arabic_text: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا
verses.translation_en: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does this verse say about the favors of Allah?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: They are beyond counting. The verse is an invitation to notice, not to complete the count.

evidence.arabic: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا
evidence.translation_en: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them.
evidence.why_cited: It states the limit of counting.

evidence.translation_en: And He gave you from all you asked of Him.

verses.translation_en: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What is the dua of Sulaiman?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: He asks Allah to enable him to be grateful. Gratitude itself is asked for as a gift.

evidence.translation_en: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor.
evidence.why_cited: It shows gratitude is sought from Allah.

evidence.translation_en: And to do righteousness that pleases You.

verses.translation_en: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?

socratic_dropdowns.question: Why is this verse repeated in Surah Ar-Rahman?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It is repeated thirty-one times. Each time, it comes after a description of mercy. The repetition is the message.

evidence.arabic: الرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ
evidence.translation_en: The Most Compassionate, taught the Quran, created man, and taught him eloquence.
evidence.why_cited: It lists favors before the question is asked.

evidence.translation_en: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
evidence.why_cited: It is the refrain after every favor.
